title: Investigation scorecard and dashboard storyflow
content:
Purpose

This doc proposes a lightweight, repeatable investigation scorecard + dashboard storyflow to help oncall and engineers move from alert -> hypothesis -> confirmation faster for inference incidents. The aim is to reduce mean-time-to-insight by standardizing which micro-widgets we assemble, what traces to pull, and how to score severity for prioritization and postmortems.

Overview of the approach

1) Quick triage scorecard (first 5–15 minutes) — a single-line summary and 6 axis score (0–3 each):
   - User impact (0 none, 3 widespread degraded responses)
   - SLI delta (observed reduction in success/latency SLOs)
   - Reproducibility (0 intermittent, 3 reproducible on demand)
   - Cost/throughput risk (token surge, unexpected GPU use)
   - Model-quality signal (increase in hallucination or rejection)
   - Investigability (trace availability, span density)

   Total >9 -> page escalation; 5–9 -> engage triage; <5 -> monitor. Keep the scoring in the alert card and add to incident ticket metadata (ENG-).

2) Dashboard storyflow (what to assemble first)

   Stage A — impact surface (single pane):
     - Global SLI sparklines (99p latency, p50/p95 for token generation)
     - Token-in / token-out rate heatmap by customer tier
     - Request success rate and error-class breakdown (model errors, infra, rate-limit)

   Stage B — candidate root buckets (microdashlets):
     - Routing & fallback: percentage of requests routed to fallback models and latency of fallbacks
     - KV cache warmth index: rolling warmth by tenant and model variant (cold vs warm percentiles)
     - Batching pressure: queue length, batching window, batch size distribution
     - Resource contended nodes: GPU utilization per pod and slowest-kernel traces

   Stage C — trace evidence pane (correlation map):
     - Trace anchors: show 3 representative traces for each candidate bucket (routing, cold cache, batch stall)
     - Span-level waterfall with annotation for model kernels, kv cache hits, and network waits
     - Correlation matrix: short traces (<=200ms) vs long traces (>2s) with feature flags and model hash overlay

3) Microdashlet templates (quick copy)

   - Incident header: title, triage score, links to ticket + slack thread, last-modified owner
   - Time-slice chooser: fast selector (1m/5m/30m/6h) with auto-aligned incident window
   - Error union widget: union of top 6 error-types with temporal stacking and sample message
   - Trace gallery: 3 columns (fastest, median, slowest) auto-populated by quantile selector

4) Runbook steps (operator-first checklist)

   0. Capture triage score and create incident ticket (tag: obs/triage).
   1. Open Stage A pane; confirm user impact and SLI delta windows.
   2. Toggle Stage B microdashlets one-by-one to see which bucket moves with the incident window.
   3. If a candidate bucket spikes, open Trace evidence pane and fetch 3 representative traces. Attach trace ids to ticket.
   4. If KV-warmth is low for impacted tenants, run cache-warm probe (internal script: /scripts/probe-kv-warmth) and document results.
   5. If batching windows increased, collect batch sizes and inspect worker logs for serialization stalls (log grep patterns: BATCH_WAIT, KV_LOCK).

5) Trace correlation map rules

   - Prefer trace sampling + annotation for long path spans (>500ms). If sampling budget is constrained, prioritize traces that include model-run spans.
   - Use consistent trace tags: model_hash, tenant_id, route_version, batch_id. Ensure these fields are present in 95% of traces in the next rollout.
   - Correlate by tag first (fast grouping), then by path timings. Present a small coalesced view for the operator: top 3 root causes with confidence score.

6) Post-incident artifacts

   - Attach final triage scorecard, top 6 supporting widgets, and trace gallery to the postmortem.
   - Add a one-line remediation ask (e.g., pin fallback, increase trace sampling for route X).
   - If runbook step required code change, create a backlog ticket and include metric/regression tests.

Open questions / TODOs

   - Threshold tuning: what absolute SLI delta should force paging for different tiers? (enterprise vs free).
   - Widget runtime cost: can we cache the microdashlets to reduce query load during incidents? (see GH PR 98).
   - Trace tag coverage: partner with serving-runtime to ensure model_hash and batch_id are included in all spans by Q2.

Notes to self / quick links

   - Slack thread: #ops-incidents — keep a running short summary in the thread header.
   - Quick query snippets: saved dashboards prefixed obs/inc- for fast clone.
   - Example incident: ENG-1179 shows a triage score of 11 where cache coldness + batch stall were both present; attach here for template reuse.

Quick operator cheatsheet (1-liner)

   - Score first, assemble Stage A, toggle Stage B microdashlets, fetch traces, attach evidence, propose immediate mitigation, and create followups.
